name: How to Plan Your Vanity Installation: A Step-by-Step Guide

step.name: Step 1: Measure Everything, Twice
step.text: Before you even think about buying, grab your tape measure. You need accurate wall width, available depth, and critical door and drawer clearances. Don’t forget to note your existing drain and supply line locations, as these dictate a lot about what new vanity will fit without major plumbing work. Consider countertop height, too, for maximum comfort.

step.name: Step 2: Prepare Your Space
step.text: First things first: shut off and disconnect the water to your old vanity. You’ll then carefully remove the existing unit, making sure to contain any residual water from the trap. This is also a good time to assess the condition of your walls and flooring; address any necessary repairs now, especially if there's old water damage.

step.name: Step 3: Locate Wall Studs and Plan Openings
step.text: If your new vanity is wall-mounted, or even if it’s freestanding, you’ll need to locate wall studs for secure fastening. For plumbing, mark and carefully cut only the necessary openings in the back of the new cabinet for the pipes. Resist the urge to make them too large, as this can compromise stability and appearance.

step.name: Step 4: Position and Level the New Vanity
step.text: Carefully maneuver the new vanity into place. Use a level to ensure it's perfectly level both side-to-side and front-to-back. Shims can be your best friend here! Once leveled, secure the cabinet to the wall studs using appropriate fasteners. This step is critical for a stable and long-lasting installation.

step.name: Step 5: Install Countertop, Sink, and Faucet
step.text: With the cabinet secure, it's time for the countertop. Install it according to manufacturer instructions, then drop in your new sink and mount the faucet. Make sure all connections are tight before moving on. This sequence ensures everything is sealed properly before water is reintroduced.

step.name: Step 6: Reconnect and Test Plumbing
step.text: Reconnect the supply lines and the P-trap to your new sink and faucet. Once everything is snugly connected, gradually restore the water supply. It's crucial to test all connections thoroughly for leaks. Don't call it done until you've checked every joint and let the water run for a bit. If you’re unsure at any stage, especially with plumbing or wall structure, bringing in a professional like Frasheski Construction can save you a lot of headaches (and potential water damage!).
